title: 2007 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: A set of \(25\) square blocks is arranged into a \(5\times 5\) square. How many different combinations of \(3\) blocks can be selected from that set so that no two are in the same row or column?

solutions.text:
Choose \(3\) of the \(5\) rows in \(\binom{5}{3}=10\) ways and \(3\) of the \(5\) columns in \(\binom{5}{3}=10\) ways.

The three chosen blocks must occupy distinct rows and columns, so they form a matching between the three rows and three columns, which can be done in \(3!=6\) ways.

The total is \(10\cdot 10\cdot 6=600.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Choose which \(3\) rows and which \(3\) columns are used
After picking \(3\) rows and \(3\) columns, the blocks correspond to a matching between them
